First and whole-order end: EO 12379 section 20, which revokes EO 12083 "as amended" (1982-08-17, read as on signing), because the amendment has no operation once the order it amends is revoked; EO 12121 is not named by number, which the clause reason states with the alternative reading. Later event: the EO 12156 further amendment of the same section. No. 12121, Feb. 26, 1979, 44 F.R. 11195" and by EO 12148, "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12379, § 20, Aug. 17, 1982, 47 F.R. 36100"; the eCFR machine search records none. The note gives no effective date and the statute is not held, so the date the Director's office ceased is not fixed by a held source beyond falling in or after 1981 and before EO 12379. (2) The Council on Wage and Price Stability. An editorial note in the held 1989 codification text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12154.txt, sha256 bff5d25514c124e6fc4decb93eeae7ae824204d396dcb03bca755207208da54a) states that "The Council on Wage and Price Stability was abolished by Execu-" tive Order 12288 of Jan. 29, 1981. research_rationale: EO 11436 (signed 1968-12-02; 33 FR 17943, Federal Register of December 4, 1968) suspends section 6372 of title 10, United States Code (retirement or retention on the active list of certain rear admirals in the Navy), citing as its sole authority "section 6386 (c) of title 10" of the United States Code. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11436.txt, PDF page 7); its number, title and the December 4, 1968 issue line match the census register row, but the extracted text prints no page number, so I did not confirm the page 17943 citation from it. Its single operative sentence is the whole order, and it states no duration. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; that express revocation is the first end. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither is the end because neither names EO 11436): (1) the National Emergencies Act, Pub. L. 94-412 (Sept. 14, 1976), whose section 101(a) terminated, two years after enactment, powers possessed as a result of national emergencies then in effect; its section 502(a)(8) provides that the Act shall not apply to "Sections 3313, 6386(c), and 8313 of title 10, United States" Code, so that termination did not reach the section 6386(c) authority this order rests on (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10976_Pub._L._94-412_National_Emergencies_Act_sec._101_a_90_Stat._1255_Sept._14_1976_status_d1e4940870.txt, text sha256 9af91c5062c556d26e97baaad68d89a4aa6cbfbb51937898bc13ef801d78a350). (2) The Defense Officer Personnel Management Act, Pub. L. 96-513 (Dec. 12, 1980), whose section 335 provides that "The following sections of chapter 573 are repealed:" and lists, among others, sections 6372 (the section this order suspends) and 6386 (the section whose subsection (c) is the order's authority), effective September 15, 1981 under section 701(a) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11436_Defense_Officer_Personnel_Management_Act_Pub._L._96-513_Dec._12_1980_94_Stat._2835_in_bdcccb89ac.txt, text sha256 c3ab6a35c6abc89d1a7cf8da82a3857809878054424edc8731240edb46dc7970). Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed, so it does not apply to the repealed section 6372; section 703 preserves matured rights, penalties and proceedings. After September 15, 1981 the suspension had no statutory provision left to operate on, but under the ruling the repeal is a disclosed candidate, and the order's end remains the instrument that names it. The pre-1981 text of 10 U.S.C. 6372 and 6386(c) is not held, so no statutory duration limit on the suspension is shown either way.
